title: Presentation pass: explorable tables, computed language measures

focus.title: 17% interchangeable, 45% cite nothing
focus.ask: Two new measures, both computed rather than judged. 17% of agent2agent messages sit no closer in vocabulary to their own thread than to any other; 45% cite nothing checkable. Is this the picture of the list you were describing, or is it measuring something adjacent to it?

focus.title: Only 2 of 7 properties replicate across both lists
focus.ask: The callout is now derived from the table rather than written beside it. Asking a question and already having standing are the only properties that clear 0.15 on both lists in the same direction. Everything else moves on one list only. Does that read as the finding, or as hedging?

focus.title: 7 of 45 topics carry a name at once
focus.ask: Labels are now placed greedily so none overlap, which means most topics are unnamed until you hover or zoom in. Is that the right trade against the previous state, where 28 of 45 names printed on top of each other?

focus.title: 301 of 392 threads are too short to measure
focus.ask: Thread-level language measures are withheld below four messages, because a two-message thread's similarity to its own thread is one comparison and it dominated the sort. That leaves 91 threads with those columns. Is a four-message floor right, or does it hide the short exchanges you most want to see?
